comparison: Both strongly support the finding that Wnt/PCP disruption (ΔDEP-GFP) uncouples PS extension from polonaise movements. OpenEval evaluates C28-C38 with statistical support (p=0.026), while peer reviewers praise the challenging electroporation technique and PIV analyses. Both agree the experimental design appropriately demonstrates uncoupling. Peer review additionally includes C74 and C85 (model claims) in this evaluation.

Both strongly support the aphidicolin mitotic arrest findings. OpenEval evaluates C39-C55 as comprehensively demonstrating uncoupling with dose-dependent effects and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'convincing evidence' with strong statistical support (p=0.0038). Both agree early polonaise movements are maintained without PS extension. Peer review additionally includes C87 (model claim) in this evaluation.

Both strongly support the ectopic Vg1/COS cell findings. OpenEval evaluates C56-C64 as demonstrating secondary PS induction and reprogrammed cell flow. Peer reviewers describe this as 'the most creative' approach and 'elegant addition' showing disruption of authentic polonaise without affecting PS elongation. Both agree the experimental design with appropriate controls supports the conclusions. Peer review additionally includes C80-C81 (discussion claims) in this evaluation.

Perfect agreement on C65-C70. Both strongly support the combined aphidicolin + Vg1/COS findings demonstrating Vg1's capability to induce cell flow independent of PS extension. OpenEval highlights strong statistical support (p=0.0005×10⁻³) and maintenance of polonaise at induced axis. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall uncoupling demonstration through independent approaches, with Reviewer 1 explicitly stating Vg1 elicits both processes in parallel without interdependence.

Both support the overall interpretive model (C7-C8, C88) that PS extension and polonaise movements can be uncoupled. OpenEval evaluates this as a logical integration of experimental results from all three manipulations. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the uncoupling model, with the editor stating extension and movements 'can be uncoupled' and reviewers accepting the proposed model. However, peer review focuses on fewer claims (C7, C8, C55, C88) while OpenEval includes additional model claims (C74-C75, C85, C87).

Both evaluate C82-C83 as UNCERTAIN regarding dose-dependent Vg1 effects. OpenEval notes these are speculative inferences without direct experimental evidence, though reasonable. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly questions this interpretation and suggests testing by reducing COS cell mass, indicating this would be 'preferable to incorporate' but acknowledges authors propose it for future investigations. Both agree this represents a gap in current evidence requiring additional experiments.

Partial overlap on C76-C78 (myosin discussion claims). OpenEval evaluates C27, C71-C73, C76-C79, C84, C86, C89 as SUPPORTED background/discussion context with appropriate citations. Peer review evaluates C52, C76-C78 as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 identifying incomplete data on myosin cable effects under ΔDEP and Vg1 perturbations. The disagreement reflects different scopes: OpenEval assesses appropriateness of cited literature while peer review identifies gaps in experimental investigation of myosin mechanisms.

Minimal overlap on C52 only. OpenEval evaluates C52 and C90 as SUPPORTED acknowledgments of limitations with appropriate citations. Peer review evaluates C52, C76-C78 as UNCERTAIN, identifying incomplete myosin cable data as a weakness. Both recognize gaps in knowledge, but OpenEval views the acknowledgment as appropriate framing while peer review emphasizes the need for additional experimental investigation.

OpenEval evaluates C1, C9-C24 as SUPPORTED background claims with appropriate citations establishing context for gastrulation, cell flows, and PS development. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/background claims.
OpenEval evaluates C91-C93 as SUPPORTED standard methodological procedures with appropriate documentation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methods claims.
